record.paper_title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation
record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant k such that for every positive integer q there is an integer a coprime to q whose finite continued fraction expansion a/q = [b_0; b_1, ..., b_s] has all partial quotients b_j, for j >= 1, bounded by k? Zaremba's original stronger guess is that k = 5 suffices.

evidence.quote: For an irreducible rational fraction aq ∈ Q we consider its continued fraction expansion a/q = [b0 ; b1 , . . . , bs ]

The famous Zaremba’s conjecture [154] supposes that there exists an absolute constant k with the following property: for any positive integer q there exists a coprime to q such that in the continued fraction expansion (53) all partial quotients are bounded
In fact Zaremba conjectured that k = 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a rational number a/q in lowest terms with q a positive integer, write its finite continued fraction expansion as
   a/q = [b_0; b_1, b_2, …, b_s] := b_0 + 1/(b_1 + 1/(b_2 + 1/(… + 1/b_s))),
where b_0 ∈ ℤ and b_1, …, b_s are positive integers (the partial quotients).

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant k (independent of q) such that for every positive integer q there exists an integer a with gcd(a, q) = 1 whose continued fraction expansion a/q = [b_0; b_1, …, b_s] satisfies
   max_{1 ≤ j ≤ s} b_j ≤ k ?

The stronger form of the question asks whether k = 5 suffices.
artifact.status_search_result: Zaremba's conjecture remains open. Significant progress was made by Bourgain and Kontorovich (2014), who proved that the set of denominators q admitting such an a with partial quotients bounded by an absolute constant has density 1, and subsequent work by Huang, Kan, Frolenkov–Kan, and others has improved various aspects, but the full conjecture (and the stronger k = 5 form) is not established.

status_evidence.title: On Zaremba's conjecture (Bourgain–Kontorovich)
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that the set of denominators satisfying Zaremba's conjecture with a fixed alphabet has positive density (in fact density one for large enough alphabet).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture itself is unresolved; only density results are known.

status_evidence.title: Zaremba's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Zaremba's conjecture is an unsolved problem in number theory about continued fractions with bounded partial quotients.
